title: Stabilizing Modality Gap & Lowering Gradient Norms Improve Zero-Shot Adversarial Robustness of VLMs

problem.claim: Vision-language models remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks despite offering zero-shot classification.

gap.claim: Robust CLIP fine-tuning typically attacks only the vision branch and uses static text prompts, limiting robustness from dual-modality fine-tuning.

contributions.claim: The approach stabilizes the modality gap and lowers or stabilizes gradient norms during CLIP fine-tuning, using both visual and text adversaries.
For both modalities, the approach maximizes the effective rank of features and modulates feature noise through count sketching.
The authors report improved zero-shot adversarial robustness and state-of-the-art performance across 15 datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report outperforming the state of the art on 15 datasets.
The authors report that maximizing feature effective rank lowers and stabilizes the modality gap across adversaries with varying perturbation radii.
The authors report that count sketching lowers and stabilizes gradient norms.

narrative_sequence.summary: VLMs provide zero-shot classification but remain vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
Existing robust CLIP fine-tuning focuses on vision-only adversaries and static text prompts, limiting dual-modality robustness.
The method targets modality-gap stability and gradient-norm stability, with further gains from visual and text adversaries.
It uses effective-rank maximization and feature-noise modulation, including count sketching.
The authors report state-of-the-art results on 15 datasets and first insights into modality gap and gradient norms.

source_observation.claim: The authors report that stabilizing the modality gap and gradient norms improves zero-shot adversarial robustness.

interpretation.claim: Robustness during multimodal fine-tuning may depend on controlling cross-modal feature geometry and optimization dynamics.

application.claim: When adapting multimodal models for adversarial robustness, monitor modality alignment and gradient-norm stability alongside task performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these effects generalize beyond CLIP fine-tuning or the reported datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, attack procedures, perturbation settings, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the effective-rank objective or count sketching.
